question: Gate G2 requires the dominant decode cost to be IDENTIFIED by measurement, not assumed. What is it?
answer: Per-access SHA-256 re-verification on the native dense/row weight paths. It is a constant per-token tax of ~2.6x, not a warm-up cost, and it is a caching defect rather than a property of the codec or the hardware.

measurements.shape: context 4, 80 decode tokens, per-token curve, 32 GiB cache budget

why_the_constant_ratio_is_the_proof: If verification were a first-touch cost it would decay as the cache filled, and the warm ratio would collapse toward 1.0. It does not: 2.62x cold and 2.63x warm. A cost that does not decay with cache occupancy is being paid per access, not per tensor. Residency, measured independently, contributes only ~9-10 percent and behaves exactly as a warm-up cost should.
root_cause_confirmed_in_source: gravity_glm.rs: GpuWeightCache's WeightAccess impl routes dense() and row() straight to self.weights, bypassing the GPU cache entirely. Only matvec and matvec_batch go through ensure().
gravity.rs ~875: GravityWeights::dense() in the Lazy branch calls shard.read_tensor(name, *verify_hash) on EVERY call with no memoization; row() has the same shape.
read_tensor recomputes a full SHA-256 of the payload each time.

Those tensors are norms and biases, which the code's own comment says are 'touched every layer'. 78 layers x several tensors x every token means the same handful are re-read, re-widened and re-hashed thousands of times per run.
why_the_original_reasoning_missed_it: The comment justifying the bypass argues that decoding small native tensors on the CPU each call is cheaper than a GPU read-back round trip. That is true and remains true. It simply never accounted for re-verification riding along on every access.
controller_correction: I predicted verification would stop mattering in the warm window because it is once-per-tensor. That was right for the matvec path and wrong for the two paths that skip the cache. The measurement contradicted the prediction and the source confirmed the measurement.

what_is_available.mechanism: Memoize the decoded native tensors so each is read, widened and verified once per process.
what_is_available.integrity_constraint: Verification must still happen AT LEAST ONCE per tensor per process. The guarantee is that bytes were checked before use; the defect is that they are checked repeatedly, not that checking is wrong. A fix that simply stops verifying would be a regression disguised as a speedup.
what_is_available.status: Fix delegated. The controller will re-run this same 80-token benchmark and report the delta rather than accepting a claimed one.

g2_standing: The dominant decode cost is now identified by measurement, as the gate requires. BASE_TRUE_TPS is stated with cold and warm as separate windows and residency alongside. What remains for G2 is re-measuring after the memo fix lands.
not_evidence_of: that the memoization fix achieves the full 2.6x -- nothing has been rebuilt or re-measured yet
